column6: Jujur, kalau lewat Terminal Ferry Batam Centre ini emang kerasa banget vibe-nya sibuk. Namanya juga gerbang utama internasional, jadi jangan kaget kalau suasananya selalu hectic, apalagi pas akhir pekan atau jam-jam keberangkatan feri. Buat saya pribadi, nilai plusnya di sini adalah lokasinya yang sudah terintegrasi langsung dengan mal. Jadi, kalau nunggu keberangkatan, nggak mati gaya—tinggal nyeberang dikit udah bisa cari makan atau sekadar ngadem. Itu ngebantu banget sih buat kill time. Tapi ya, konsekuensinya harus siap mental sama antrean imigrasi yang kadang bisa panjang banget. Saran saya, jangan mepet kalau mau berangkat, harus kasih jeda waktu yang cukup biar nggak keteteran. Secara fasilitas, tempat ini tergolong fungsional—nggak yang mewah-mewah banget, tapi sudah cukup oke untuk kebutuhan mobilitas rutin. Overall, buat ukuran terminal sibuk, tempat ini lumayan bisa diandalkan asal kita paham manajemen waktunya

column6: I rated so low, not because of the architecture, but because of the immigration officers at there. they are like robbers. they see your passport and without a reason and ask you to wait in a place, especially to those people who come from lower income country and cannot communicate in English well. they ask for up to 300 Singapore dollars upon various reasons. even though Southeast Asia passport holders do not need visa for entering Indonesia, the immigration officers at the Batam make excuses about not having visitors visa or maybe regarding return flights from other countries such as Singapore. No one will overstay at that small island but they are so dangerous and asked for money. They frighten you in various ways including using phone in waiting area. A lot of people from Malaysia Singapore and from Myanmar have experiences like that and be extra careful about these immigration officers who ask for money at the Batam ferry terminal immigration. For me, I counter questioned them with good commend in English. There is no way I will pay for ridiculous reason while I am a globetrotter with various experiences. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Batam Centre Fast Ferry Terminal cukup ramai karena menjadi salah satu pintu utama keluar masuk Batam, terutama untuk rute internasional seperti ke Singapura dan Johor. Lokasinya strategis, dekat dengan pusat kota dan beberapa pusat perbelanjaan. Area terminal cukup luas dan fasilitas dasar seperti tempat duduk, loket tiket, serta pemeriksaan imigrasi tersedia dengan baik. Namun saat jam sibuk antrean bisa cukup panjang dan suasana terasa padat. Secara keseluruhan terminal ini cukup memadai untuk perjalanan laut, meskipun kenyamanan bisa lebih ditingkatkan saat ramai.

column6: Pagi-Pagi ke sini untuk menyebrang ke spore. Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan salah satu gerbang utama bagi wisatawan dan pebisnis yang ingin menyeberang ke Singapura dan Malaysia. Sebagai pelabuhan internasional yang sibuk, tempat ini dikenal dengan suasana yang tertib dan kondusif, memberikan kenyamanan bagi para penumpang yang akan berangkat maupun yang baru tiba. Salah satu hal yang paling mencolok di Pelabuhan Batam Center adalah sistem antrian dan pengelolaan penumpangnya yang teratur. Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian. Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan. Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya.

column6: Waktu kunjungan: Desember 2024 Dibandingkan dengan pelabuhan Harbour Bay, pelabuhan ini lebih kecil, tetapi tidak kalah ramai karena melayani wilayah pusat pemerintahan Batam dan pemukiman di sekitarnya. Karena hal ini juga, ukuran terminal terasa terlalu kecil dan sumpek. Tidak terbayang seberapa kecil ruang tunggu pascapemeriksaan imigrasi - mungkin strategi menyempatkan waktu sesedikit mungkin hal yang baik jika berangkat dari pelabuhan ini. Proses pemeriksaan kedatangan imigrasi lancar dan efisien, tidak ada masalah - petugas bahkan mengajak bercanda sejenak, mungkin untuk melepaskan kejemuan pekerjaan yang repetitif. Di dalam terminal pelabuhan, cukup banyak kios makanan dan tentunya suvenir, serta bahkan supermarket kecil. Bangunan terhubung langsung dengan mall besar melalui jembatan pejalan kaki. Cukup cari pintu akses di lantai dua bangunan pelabuhan, yang ditandai jelas.

Tidak terbayang seberapa kecil ruang tunggu pascapemeriksaan imigrasi - mungkin strategi menyempatkan waktu sesedikit mungkin hal yang baik jika berangkat dari pelabuhan ini. Proses pemeriksaan kedatangan imigrasi lancar dan efisien, tidak ada masalah - petugas bahkan mengajak bercanda sejenak, mungkin untuk melepaskan kejemuan pekerjaan yang repetitif. Di dalam terminal pelabuhan, cukup banyak kios makanan dan tentunya suvenir, serta bahkan supermarket kecil. Bangunan terhubung langsung dengan mall besar melalui jembatan pejalan kaki. Cukup cari pintu akses di lantai dua bangunan pelabuhan, yang ditandai jelas.

column6: Very bad experience at Batam Centre Immigration. My wife and young daughter were stopped while using the autogate at Batam Centre Ferry Terminal and taken into a private office. Their phones were taken away, leaving them unable to contact me while my friends and I waited outside for almost one hour without knowing what happened. They were told they could not enter Indonesia but no clear reason was given. My young daughter was crying because she did not understand what she had done wrong. The officers then hinted that the problem could be “solved” and asked for USD 100 per person. After saying she had no cash, they even suggested transferring money. Eventually they allowed her to contact me to bring cash. My wife and daughter were released only after we paid SGD 200. This experience strongly suggests corrupt behaviour and abuse of authority. Because of this incident, my friends and I will strongly not recommend our friends and family to visit Batam. Normally, I leave tips when I travel, but this trip I left zero tips because the immigration experience completely spoiled our trip. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Good ferry terminal. The place seems dated but the place is good enough. The ferry ticketing office is on the ground floor, very accessible from the main entrance. They have some food and a convenience store in the second floor. The food is quite good. The immigration process works very good on the outbound, though the inbound is slower as they didn’t have the automated gates. The problem with the place is the transportation is monopolized by port taxi which is very expensive which charged around twice compared to ride-sharing apps. Ride-sharing apps won’t pick you up at the lobby because of the monopoly, you have to walk out to the gates if you wanted to get one - which can be a problem if it’s raining. The other alternative is to cross the pedestrian bridge to the mall and get the ride-share from there. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: ⭐ 1/5 — Worst Travel Experience Ever. Detained Without a Clear Reason. I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

I have travelled extensively across Europe, Turkey and Southeast Asia, and I can confidently say that this was the worst travel experience I have ever had. My wife, our child and I travelled to Batam with friends for a simple weekend getaway. We cleared Malaysian Immigration, received our departure clearance and boarded the ferry without any issue. The moment we arrived at the Batam ferry terminal, a police officer approached us, took our passports and brought our family into a room. Later, our child was allowed to leave with our friends while my wife and I were kept there. We were made to wait for almost TWO HOURS with no proper explanation. Only after we repeatedly demanded answers were we told that we were being detained because the Malaysian police had supposedly requested it. That explanation made absolutely no sense. If Malaysian authorities had actually placed any restriction on us, how did we clear Malaysian Immigration and legally depart Malaysia without any problem? The whole situation ruined our trip. We no longer felt comfortable staying in Batam, so we choose to return to Malaysia immediately. Here is the most shocking part. When we arrived back in Malaysia, Malaysian Immigration interviewed us. We explained everything and asked what case or issue had caused us to be detained in Batam. They could not identify any reason for it. There appeared to be no case or immigration issue involving either of us. They were also puzzled as to why we had been detained after we had already cleared Malaysian Immigration normally. So I would genuinely like to know: Why were we detained for almost two hours? Why were we separated from our child without a clear explanation? Why were we told that Malaysian police had requested our detention when Malaysian authorities could not identify the reason for it? Being detained in a foreign country without being clearly told why, especially while travelling with your child, is not something any traveller should have to experience. What was supposed to be a relaxing weekend getaway turned into an extremely stressful and disturbing experience. I am sharing this so other travellers are aware of what happened to us, and I sincerely hope the relevant authorities investigate and provide a proper explanation. For us, this was completely unacceptable and easily the worst travel experience we have ever had. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Corruption Alert at Batam Centre Ferry Terminal Customs (13 March 2026) Arrived at Batam Centre via evening ferry from HarbourFront and experienced blatant extortion by customs officers. While queuing for passport clearance, we moved to a shorter autogate line. An officer stopped us and escorted us to a hidden “interrogation room” out of public view. Inside, several foreigners were already waiting. One by one, we were called in. A Filipino traveller before us was forced to pay a “penalty” over her passport condition. When it was our turn, my partner came out saying: “They want money.” Inside the interrogation room, I was accused by two officers of a “disrespectful offence” for allegedly crossing a barrier. The officers shouted, confiscated my phone, intimidated, and demanded SGD 100 penalty per person. I was threatened with two options: pay immediately or be detained overnight and forced to return to Singapore the next day. After 1.5 hours of unjustified intimidation, threats and pressure, we paid the penalty despite not committing any wrongdoing. This was not enforcement. This was coercion and extortion targeting travellers. I will seriously reconsider ever returning to Batam. To all Travellers, do note that being cautious may not be helpful as you could be forced to pay penalty for any possible reason. Perhaps pray for better luck or avoiding Batam at all costs will be a better choice. Stay safe and good luck guys. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

If you’re considering booking with Sindo Ferry, I recommend being very careful and confirming the change policy in advance. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: CORRUPTION! This incident really scarred my experience going to Batam. My partner and I were 'detained' in a room along with many others of different nationalities (SG, MY, PH, BD, CN etc.), each with different minor/non-issues, and none of us were told any reasons for being detained for at least an hour. They took our passport and put it in an empty room. After waiting for more than an hour, the officers finally called us into the room, 1 at a time. They started shouting, "DO YOU KNOW WHAT YOU DID WRONG?!, THAT IS VERY DISRESPECTFUL!" of course, none of us knew initially what was wrong, until they gave a reason (which can literally be anything). After shouting and trying their best to instill fear, while smoking and vaping at the same time, they presented us with 2 options: 1. Go back to Singapore on the next ferry (which was the next day since there were no more ferries that night) 2. Pay the fine of sgd100 each. The officers were never going to let us go without payment, and I started to see many others paying up as they were detained for hours. We eventually gave in and paid the 'fine', after 2 hours. This was when we saw a stack of cash under the keyboard in their interrogation room. Extremely terrifying experience and blatant act of corruption. All the officers are in cahoots, and it seems like a common thing for all of them. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Absolutely horrible and corrupt experience at immigration arriving from HarbourFront Terminal to Batam Centre. Happened on 14 February 2026, around 1pm - 330pm. I was detained over a so-called “spoiled” passport even though I had just travelled internationally with zero issues. When I tried to explain, the officer was rude and dismissive, saying “This is Indonesia, not Thailand” instead of giving any proper reason or solution. Then the most shocking part happened. I was told the immigration officer “couldn’t help” and was pushed to speak to an “agent” who offered me three choices: • Go back to Singapore • Wait for hours until they felt satisfied (possibly until night shift) • Pay a “fee” to settle it It was VERY clear they were pressuring me to pay money. This felt like bribery and abuse of power, not a legitimate immigration process. I WAS ROBBED IDR500,000. I came to Batam for charity work to help orphanages and people in need, and instead was treated like a target to squeeze money from. Completely unethical, stressful, and humiliating. This experience alone makes me never want to step foot in Batam again. Tourists should be extremely careful. This is not how immigration should ever operate. Also, pls hide your cash. They’re gg to look inside your bag to see how much you have. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: CORRUPT IMMIGRATION OFFICERS AT THIS FERRY TERMINAL IMMIGRATION On 21 February, my family and I made a plan to visit Batam, Indonesia. The Chinese New Year holiday had just passed, and we wanted a short, peaceful getaway—two days of rest and sightseeing before my mother returns to the Philippines. It was meant to be simple family time. We are Philippine passport holders - husband, myself and my daughter have valid SG long term pass. Indonesians grant 30-day visa-free entry for Philippine passport holders. We had return tickets within the allowed period. We had hotel bookings. Everything was straightforward. But the moment we reached immigration in Batam on 21 Feb 2026, 1030AM Indonesian time, things changed. We were suddenly held back and questioned. The officers accused us of traveling to Batam “only to extend my mom’s visa in Singapore.” This accusation shocked us. Why would Indonesian immigration be concerned about Singapore’s ICA policies? We were entering Indonesia legally under Indonesia’s visa-free scheme. We were not overstaying anywhere. We were not violating any Indonesian law. Despite explaining that this was a short 2-day leisure trip, we were escorted into an office for further “interrogation.” The room was poorly lit and tense. There were other tourists inside as well, including an Indian passport holder who also appeared distressed. The atmosphere felt intimidating. Questions were repeated. The tone was accusatory, as if we had already done something wrong. Then the officer’s tone changed. He told us we had “two options”: 1. Change my mother’s flight and book her a ticket back to the Philippines on a date they wanted. 2. Pay SGD 150 as a “penalty” for “transiting” in Batam. Penalty for what violation? There was no clear explanation. No written notice. No official receipt mentioned upfront. No formal charge. Just two “options.” Why should Indonesian immigration dictate when my mother flies back to the Philippines? Why was there a “penalty” when we were within Indonesia’s visa-free entry rules? At that moment, fear took over. We were in a foreign immigration office. We saw how the officer spoke to other tourists. We did not know what could happen next—would they deny entry? Cancel our passports? Blacklist us? Create further complications for our travel? Feeling intimidated and powerless, and wanting to avoid further trouble, we agreed to pay the money. What was supposed to be a relaxing family trip turned into a deeply stressful and unsettling experience. It leaves travelers questioning: 1. Are short leisure trips now suspicious? 2. Is visiting Batam after staying in Singapore automatically treated as wrongdoing? 3. Why are tourists pressured with vague “penalties” without clear written violations? Experiences like this damage trust. Tourism thrives on safety, fairness, and transparency. When travelers feel intimidated or pressured without clear legal basis, it creates fear—not confidence. We came for rest and sightseeing. We left with disappointment. This will likely be our last visit to Batam. To fellow travelers: always keep your documents complete, know your visa rules, and stay calm—but also be aware of your rights. No holiday should begin with fear. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Batam Centre Point International Ferry Terminal - Functional But Basic Location: Batam Centre, Kota Batam, Kepulauan Riau Rating: ⭐⭐⭐ (3.5/5) I've passed through this terminal several times over the past year, so I've gotten pretty familiar with how it operates. The Good: The basics are covered well enough. There are plenty of SIM card kiosks right when you arrive, which is handy if you need to get connected immediately. Immigration processing is straightforward - nothing fancy, but it moves along at a reasonable pace. Luggage retrieval is simple and easy to navigate. The real bonus is the overhead walkway that connects directly to Mega City Mall. Makes getting to the Grab taxi stand super convenient - you don't have to deal with touts or figure out where to go. Just walk across and you're there. The Not-So-Good: It's a functional terminal, but that's about it. Don't expect much in terms of amenities or comfort while you're waiting. The facility feels pretty basic and could use some updating to make the arrival/departure experience more pleasant. Bottom Line: Does the job for getting in and out of Batam, and the connection to Mega City Mall is genuinely useful for onward travel. It's not going to wow you, but it won't give you major headaches either. If you're a regular traveler to Batam like me, you'll appreciate the straightforward layout even if it's nothing special. column2: Batam Centre Point International Ferry Terminal
column6: Hey guys, it’s your favorite elite traveler back with another unfiltered review—and this time, we need to talk about the gatekeeping situation at the Batam Center Ferry Terminal. As an Indonesian who travels extensively, I am usually so proud to welcome international visitors to our beautiful country. But my recent arrival at Batam Center at PM was, without exaggeration, an absolute NIGHTMARE. If this terminal is meant to be a major international gateway, the current reality is a total embarrassment to our national hospitality. Here is the raw truth about what you can expect if you land here late at night: 1. The Immigration Bottle-Neck (The Absolute Worst Part) Imagine an entire ferry of exhausted travelers arriving at PM, only to find exactly one immigration officer working the counter. The inefficiency was mind-boggling. But the real vibe-killer was the officer handling the desk—an older woman named Ibu May. To say she was rude is an understatement. Unprofessional, highly inefficient, and frankly, throwing what I can only describe as a 5-year-old’s tantrum behind the desk. As an Indonesian, it broke my heart to watch her. She is single-handedly ruining the image of Indonesian hospitality for every international tourist standing in that excruciatingly long line. 2. Zero Digital Readiness Before you even get to the chaos inside, there is no coordination at the entrance. There are no QR codes shared or displayed at the entrance for required digital arrivals or health forms before you enter the terminal. Everyone is left scrambling in the dark, trying to figure out what they need to do. It’s clunky, outdated, and unacceptable for a major transit hub in 2026. 3. The Transport Monopoly Trap Once you finally escape the terminal, don't even think about opening your Grab or Gojek apps. The terminal strictly bans ride-hailing apps to protect their local taxi monopoly. Normally, I’m all for supporting local drivers, but the execution here is a safety and logistical hazard. Most of the drivers stationed there are very elderly, struggle to understand directions, and—unbelievably—do not know how to type into or use Google Maps to reach your destination. If you don't know the exact streets yourself, you are essentially stranded with a driver who can't navigate. The Verdict 🚨 Batam Center Ferry Terminal needs a massive wake-up call, urgent staff retraining, and a complete tech overhaul. To the management: please address the lack of personnel, the attitude of staff like Ibu May, and let ride-hailing apps in so travelers can actually get home safely. After check in at Sindo Ferry counter, went to the Immigration Inspection, aside of boarding card, so be ready with your passport and ID (KTP). And after boarding call, walk along the departure gate to the ferry..ready to go. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column2: Batam Centre Point International Ferry Terminal
column6: Very dated International Ferry Terminal, with Arrivals on Level 1 and Departure entry on Level 2. Hassle free and smooth Arrival and Departure Customs and Immigration processes. Level 1 comprises various ferry operators' counters (for purchasing ferry tickets or check-in); money changing, Indonesian mobile SIM cards and retail concessionaires. Level 2 comprises mostly F & B, souvenir and convenience store concessionaires. The Ferry Departures check-in gates leading to the Customs and Immigration are also on Level 2. Not advisable to take a taxi from this terminal unless you are familiar with the local rates of your destination. GRAB taxis are not allowed to pick up passengers from this Terminal due to the control of the taxi cartels here. Alternatively you can proceed to Level 2 and head to the Mega Mall connected by a pedestrian bridge, and book your Grab taxi at the Mall (Lobby A next to the Starbucks). Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: We went to Batam as a group of 3 couples over the Vesak Day weekend (29 to 31/5/2026) and chose Harbour Bay terminal since it's the nearest to I-hotel Nagoya. We arrived on 29/5 around 3pm (Indo time) & auto-gate was down. Quite a number of visitors had to be transferred to the manual queue, it was quite messy with no proper management of the queues for entry. Luckily the service was quite fast & efficient. On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. Harbour Bay ferry terminal used to be smooth & less chaotic..please ensure there are sufficient officers/staff stationed at strategic points/locations in the departure area to manage the crowds. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

On 31/5, we started to head towards the departure area at 4.45pm to queue for the 5.30pm slot departure to Singapore. Although alot of passengers were milling around the departure hall - a normal sight for weekends - but the system was initially still organised & well-controlled as a staff was stationed at the start of the queue to ensure only passengers for the earliest departing ferry entered the queue. Announcements were also made both in Bahasa & English. However, the situation took a different turn after 5pm when the staff left his post unattended and the announcement for 5.30pm departure was announced together with the 5.15pm departure within a span of less than 5 minutes. Things got worse at the passport-scanning station. I was among the 1st 10-15 visitors queuing at the manual lane since there was a long queue at the auto gate. 1 of the lady officers attending to manual scanning suddenly stood & left her desk to tell us that Singapore passport-holders to queue at the auto-gate. I believe they could have managed this better by stationing officer at the queue entrance instead of directing the ones who are already in the front row to go back and join the auto-gate queue at the back. Do remember that this group consisted of passengers from 2 different vessels and there was already a congestion at the auto-gate queue due to the close interval between the 2 announcements earlier. Harbour Bay ferry terminal used to be smooth & less chaotic..please ensure there are sufficient officers/staff stationed at strategic points/locations in the departure area to manage the crowds. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: The first impression of Batam looks impressive if people do judge from this ferry terminal alone. It is indeed a very nice terminal with a lot of facilities available. The terminal is huge, clean and looks new. The immigration is smooth since it has an automated gate and all the process went well. It is a very organized terminal in a lot of aspects. There are many stores like a shopping mall that sells goods, foods and also tickets. It even has a vip lounge for a first class ticket. The ticket costs RM 80 one way and you can get cheaper if you buy a return ticket. The ticket can be bought via walk in or online from third party apps like redBUS (can get discount by using promo code) and other apps. The journey will take around 1 hour 40 minutes to Harbour Bay Batam. Do remember to standby RM 25 and 100k idr for port tax on each journey. I think there are also other destinations to go from here. I rode the dolphin ferry and it's in very good condition, clean, cold and good service All the workers are friendly and helpful. There is a deck upstairs to look for the view. Truly a good experience and memorable moments Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Terminal Harbour Bay Batam ini terminal rasa mall! Begitu masuk, langsung disambut suasana yang modern dan bersih, bikin lupa kalau ini sebenarnya terminal. Saya sampai ngerasa kayak di bandara kecil, cuma nggak ada pramugari yang siap kasih instruksi. Fasilitasnya lengkap! Mulai dari tempat duduk yang nyaman buat nunggu ferry, sampai kios-kios jajanan yang bikin perut lupa diet. Pilihan makanannya mulai dari yang ringan kayak roti sampai nasi berat—cocok buat isi tenaga sebelum perjalanan. Proses imigrasinya juga lancar. Petugasnya ramah, bikin saya nggak deg-degan meskipun paspor udah dibolak-balik kayak buku harian. Kapalnya datang dan berangkat tepat waktu, jadi nggak ada drama ‘kapan nih naiknya?’. Pemandangan di sekitar terminal juga asik. Sambil nunggu ferry, bisa liat kapal-kapal lalu lalang, rasanya kayak adegan di film perjalanan epik (padahal cuma mau nyebrang ke Singapura atau Malaysia 😆). Kesimpulan: Terminal Harbour Bay ini terminal yang nyaman, modern, dan bikin pengalaman nyebrang jadi menyenangkan. Cocok buat traveler santai atau pekerja yang sering bolak-balik Batam. Kalau ada rating untuk terminal, ini udah kayak dapet bintang Michelin versi pelabuhan!

Petugasnya ramah, bikin saya nggak deg-degan meskipun paspor udah dibolak-balik kayak buku harian. Kapalnya datang dan berangkat tepat waktu, jadi nggak ada drama ‘kapan nih naiknya?’. Pemandangan di sekitar terminal juga asik. Sambil nunggu ferry, bisa liat kapal-kapal lalu lalang, rasanya kayak adegan di film perjalanan epik (padahal cuma mau nyebrang ke Singapura atau Malaysia 😆). Kesimpulan: Terminal Harbour Bay ini terminal yang nyaman, modern, dan bikin pengalaman nyebrang jadi menyenangkan. Cocok buat traveler santai atau pekerja yang sering bolak-balik Batam. Kalau ada rating untuk terminal, ini udah kayak dapet bintang Michelin versi pelabuhan!

column6: "I am writing this to warn other international travelers to be extremely cautious when purchasing tickets at this terminal. My husband and I had a very stressful experience due to a complete lack of helpfulness and communication at the ticket counter. I came prepared with the exact name of my resort, the destination (Tanjung Pinang), and a Google Maps image showing exactly where we needed to go. While I certainly do not expect everyone to speak English, I even used a translator app on my phone to be as clear as possible. The staff member barely looked at me, refused to engage with the translator or the map, and acted as though I was a major inconvenience. Despite my best efforts to be clear, we were sold tickets to Tanjung Uban instead of Tanjung Pinang. This lack of attention meant we ended up on the wrong side of Bintan Island, resulting in a 350,000 IDR taxi fare and hours of lost travel time. In this day and age, with so many translation tools available, there is no reason for such a total breakdown in service. I hope management trains their staff to better assist tourists who are trying to communicate. Please double-check your physical ticket destination before leaving the window!" Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: [WAJIB BACA] Saya tidak suka karna pelabuhan kapal ini memonopoli harga taxi. Mereka tidak sanggup bersaing dan mendemo agar taxi online seperti grab dan gojek tidak boleh mengambil order di sini. Bahkan mereka memukul driver online & pelanggan kalau berani memesan di area pelabuhan. Mereka berkali-kali dan terus-menerus memanggil-manggil pelanggan & meminta memesan taxi mereka, di level yang sangat mengganggu. Walaupun sudah sepakat harga taxi, di tengah jalan mereka akan menaikkan harga sesuka hati dengan alasan tujuan jauh, mengintimidasi pelanggan dan memasang ekspresi wajah yang membuat pelanggan tidak nyaman. UNTUK ORANG BARU DI BATAM, APALAGI ANDA FOREIGNERS, bijaklah memilih transportasi. Ada layanan bus "trans batam" dari pemerintah, cara nya setelah keluar dari pelabuhan, jalan lurus sedikit, naik ke lantai 2 menggunakan lift/elevator atau tangga. Setelah benar-benar keluar (sampai dijalan aspal), jalan sedikit ke kiri dan terlihat halte bus. Tiket bus hanya tersedia cashless, bayar pakai QRIS. Biasanya saya turun di Mall BCS atau di area "jodoh" (persis di depan hotel pacific sekitaran harbour bay). Lanjutkan dengan memesan grab atau gojek ke tujuan anda. Saya tidak ingin membenci mereka tapi mereka sendiri yang membuat semua orang membenci mereka dengan tindakan anarkis dan pemaksaan.

column6: Kejadian kemarin saat saya hendak pulang dari Batam ke Selat Panjang melalui Pelabuhan Sekupang. Saat tiba di pelabuhan, saya menuju konter yang jelas-jelas bertuliskan “Dumai Line” untuk membeli tiket. Setelah membayar dan menerima tiket, saya heran karena tiket yang diberikan ternyata bertuliskan “Batam Jet”. Saya kemudian bertanya kepada petugas, “Kok Batam Jet? Saya mau naik Dumai Line.” Namun petugas tidak menjawab pertanyaan saya dan hanya mengatakan, “Kapal besar.” Saya kembali menegaskan bahwa saya ingin tiket Dumai Line, tetapi petugas hanya diam. Lalu petugas lain mengatakan bahwa uang tidak bisa ditransfer kembali karena pembayaran sudah dilakukan. Untungnya akhirnya uang saya dikembalikan secara tunai. Setelah itu saya membeli tiket di konter Dumai Line yang sebenarnya, yang berada tepat di sampingnya, dan mendapatkan tiket yang sesuai. Yang membuat saya semakin kesal, ternyata orang tua saya pernah mengalami kejadian serupa. Karena tidak terlalu mengenal tulisan, mereka baru mengetahui tiket yang dibeli bukan Dumai Line saat sudah hendak naik kapal dan diberitahu oleh petugas. Saya sebenarnya tidak berniat memposting hal ini. Namun karena kejadian yang sama juga dialami oleh orang tua saya, saya merasa perlu menyampaikan keluhan ini. Mohon kepada pihak Pelabuhan Sekupang untuk menindaklanjuti dan mengawasi praktik seperti ini agar tidak ada lagi penumpang yang mengalami kebingungan atau dirugikan, terutama orang tua dan penumpang yang kurang memahami perbedaan loket maupun nama operator kapal. Terima kasih.

column6: Terminal Feri Sekupang merupakan salah satu pelabuhan utama di Kota Batam yang melayani transportasi laut domestik dan internasional. Terletak di kawasan Sekupang, pelabuhan ini terbagi menjadi dua bagian, yaitu terminal domestik dan terminal internasional. Terminal domestik melayani rute antarpulau seperti ke Karimun, Tanjung Balai, Dumai, dan pulau-pulau di wilayah Riau , sementara terminal internasional melayani rute cepat ke Singapura dan Malaysia dengan waktu tempuh sekitar 45 menit. Fasilitas di Terminal Feri Sekupang tergolong lengkap dan modern. Di dalamnya tersedia ruang tunggu berpendingin udara, loket tiket yang tertata rapi, area makan dan kafe, layanan money changer, ATM, serta musholla. Tersedia juga layanan transportasi darat seperti taksi resmi dan parkir kendaraan yang luas. Terminal internasionalnya bahkan dilengkapi dengan business lounge, Wi-Fi gratis, serta sistem imigrasi yang cepat dan efisien, menjadikannya alternatif favorit bagi penumpang yang ingin menghindari keramaian di pelabuhan Batam Centre. Selain fungsi utamanya sebagai pelabuhan penumpang, Terminal Feri Sekupang juga menjadi wajah kota Batam bagi wisatawan mancanegara. Dengan tampilan bangunan yang modern dan bersih, serta layanan yang semakin profesional, terminal ini memainkan peran penting dalam mendukung sektor pariwisata dan mobilitas masyarakat. Letaknya yang strategis di dekat kawasan pemukiman seperti Tiban, Batu Aji, dan Tanjung Riau juga menjadikannya pelabuhan pilihan bagi warga lokal maupun pelancong.

column6: I work in Singapore and I took my kids and in-laws(Visit pass holders) to Batam as it was a long weekend. It was a bitter experience where my family including 2 kids(2 and 6yo) were held inside a room with no proper reason for nearly 2 hours. We waited for 15 mins clueless and realized the supposed to be officer started eating his lunch, smoking and laughing with other workers without any sense that there were older people and small kids inside that small suffocating room and I actually felt that they are obliged to attend to us first or atleast give an explanation. After all, we were not there for any free service. I stepped out because of smoke and they demanded us to stay in. We were treated no less than criminals and were literally ill treated. After an hour a guy came in and finally, I understood that they presumed that we were there for Visa extension. I was asked why we didn’t go to Malaysia, after all it was my choice to do whatever I wish and it is never mentioned anywhere in the immigration guidelines. They asked for 100$ to let us go after 1.5 hours. I asked them the passports back so that we can return, which they never did. Later, head of the immigration came, got our passports stamped and got our money back and apologised. I felt they were so racist and had some cold attitude to people from India. I will never go back again. Totally hate it, forget being an educated officer, these people are so insane that they should learn how to treat fellow human beings. Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Batam Indonesia is the most corrupt country we've ever been. Even female immigration officers will ask you for coffee money. Me and my family went there for a short vacation but little that we know that they are corrupt to the core. When we were at the immigration they held my family including my 16 year old brother in law and my wife's 11 year old niece. I was carrying our daughter for more than 20 mins waiting for them to come out from the office. My wife went to the office to ask what was the problem. The Senior Officer just straight away asked for 200sgd and couldnt even explain what is it for. Is there an entrance fee that we need to pay? Seriously? This is more corrupt than my country. Well anyway to cut the horrible story short. We bargain for the price and they let my family go for 100sgd. The only reason they gave us is because Singapore will give us another 30 more days of visit pass extension. So we have to pay the price? Nonsense. I would understand if we are looking for a job and wanted to comeback to SG but were not. And holding an 11 year old and a 16 year old? 😤Good job Batam! I will never go back there again! Never. So tourist please beware! Batam has an entrance fee! What a shame. #BatamCorrupt Lihat terjemahan (Indonesia)

column6: Jujur, kalau lewat Terminal Ferry Batam Centre ini emang kerasa banget vibe-nya sibuk. Namanya juga gerbang utama internasional, jadi jangan kaget kalau suasananya selalu hectic, apalagi pas akhir pekan atau jam-jam keberangkatan feri. Buat saya pribadi, nilai plusnya di sini adalah lokasinya yang sudah terintegrasi langsung dengan mal. Jadi, kalau nunggu keberangkatan, nggak mati gaya—tinggal nyeberang dikit udah bisa cari makan atau sekadar ngadem. Itu ngebantu banget sih buat kill time. Tapi ya, konsekuensinya harus siap mental sama antrean imigrasi yang kadang bisa panjang banget. Saran saya, jangan mepet kalau mau berangkat, harus kasih jeda waktu yang cukup biar nggak keteteran. Secara fasilitas, tempat ini tergolong fungsional—nggak yang mewah-mewah banget, tapi sudah cukup oke untuk kebutuhan mobilitas rutin. Overall, buat ukuran terminal sibuk, tempat ini lumayan bisa diandalkan asal kita paham manajemen waktunya

column6: Pagi-Pagi ke sini untuk menyebrang ke spore. Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan salah satu gerbang utama bagi wisatawan dan pebisnis yang ingin menyeberang ke Singapura dan Malaysia. Sebagai pelabuhan internasional yang sibuk, tempat ini dikenal dengan suasana yang tertib dan kondusif, memberikan kenyamanan bagi para penumpang yang akan berangkat maupun yang baru tiba. Salah satu hal yang paling mencolok di Pelabuhan Batam Center adalah sistem antrian dan pengelolaan penumpangnya yang teratur. Papan petunjuk arah tersedia dengan jelas, sehingga memudahkan pengunjung dalam mencari loket tiket, area imigrasi, dan ruang tunggu. Petugas di pelabuhan juga cukup sigap dalam membantu para penumpang, baik yang baru pertama kali datang maupun yang sudah sering bepergian. Kebersihan di area pelabuhan juga terjaga dengan baik. Fasilitas umum seperti toilet, ruang tunggu, dan area makan cukup bersih dan nyaman. Selain itu, suasana di dalam pelabuhan cenderung tertib, dengan kontrol keamanan yang ketat tetapi tetap efisien. Proses imigrasi berjalan cukup cepat, terutama jika penumpang sudah menyiapkan dokumen yang dibutuhkan. Dari segi aksesibilitas, Pelabuhan Batam Center terhubung langsung dengan pusat perbelanjaan, sehingga penumpang yang datang atau menunggu keberangkatan bisa berbelanja atau bersantap dengan nyaman. Tersedia pula berbagai moda transportasi, seperti taksi dan layanan transportasi online, yang memudahkan perjalanan ke berbagai wilayah di Batam. Secara keseluruhan, Pelabuhan Batam Center merupakan pelabuhan yang tertib, kondusif, dan memiliki fasilitas yang cukup baik. Bagi wisatawan maupun pelaku bisnis yang sering bepergian ke Singapura atau Malaysia, pelabuhan ini menjadi pilihan utama karena kepraktisan dan kenyamanan yang ditawarkannya.

column6: Terminal Harbour Bay Batam ini terminal rasa mall! Begitu masuk, langsung disambut suasana yang modern dan bersih, bikin lupa kalau ini sebenarnya terminal. Saya sampai ngerasa kayak di bandara kecil, cuma nggak ada pramugari yang siap kasih instruksi. Fasilitasnya lengkap! Mulai dari tempat duduk yang nyaman buat nunggu ferry, sampai kios-kios jajanan yang bikin perut lupa diet. Pilihan makanannya mulai dari yang ringan kayak roti sampai nasi berat—cocok buat isi tenaga sebelum perjalanan. Proses imigrasinya juga lancar. Petugasnya ramah, bikin saya nggak deg-degan meskipun paspor udah dibolak-balik kayak buku harian. Kapalnya datang dan berangkat tepat waktu, jadi nggak ada drama ‘kapan nih naiknya?’. Pemandangan di sekitar terminal juga asik. Sambil nunggu ferry, bisa liat kapal-kapal lalu lalang, rasanya kayak adegan di film perjalanan epik (padahal cuma mau nyebrang ke Singapura atau Malaysia 😆). Kesimpulan: Terminal Harbour Bay ini terminal yang nyaman, modern, dan bikin pengalaman nyebrang jadi menyenangkan. Cocok buat traveler santai atau pekerja yang sering bolak-balik Batam. Kalau ada rating untuk terminal, ini udah kayak dapet bintang Michelin versi pelabuhan!

column6: Catatan untuk naik roro (membawa kendaraan) dari punggur-ke tanjung uban melalui pelabuhan telaga punggur : 1. Untuk membeli tiket, siapkan uang dalam bentuk e-money (kartu brizzi). Bila tidak punya kartu, dapat membeli di konter yang telah disediakan (didekat gerbang masuk kendaraaan) 2. Di konter tersebut, anda juga bisa mengisi ulang kartu tersebut. 3. Selalu ingat/ memfoto plat kendaraan (karena dibutuhkan untuk syarat pembelian tiket) 4. Selalu membawa surat penting kendaraan (sim, stnk, dll) 5. Tidak membuang boarding pass (setelah pembelian tiket anda akan dapat 2/3 kertas dan salah satunya ialah kertas boarding pass yang merupakan syarat masuk kapal) 6. Setelah membeli tiket anda dapat mengantri/ membawa kendaraan ke tempat tunggu. 7. Berhati-hati saat masuk kapal.

column6: kemarin hari selasa dpt pelayanan yg buruk banget. Kita mau pesan tiket kapal yg bs bw kendaraan, dari yg jm 10 sampai 17 kuotanya udah 0 semua. Akhirnya kita brgkt ke pelabuhan buat nanya dn memastikan, sampai sana sekitar jam 9an lbh, kita tanya lah ke tmpt tiket yg di dekat ATM itu, abangnya menyambut ramah dn lgsg mengarahkan ke tmpt informasi. Sesampainya d tmpt informasi, kami tanya apa benar tiketnya udh abis semua, takutnya lg error kan, nah di tmpt informasi itu ada mbak² tp dia spt tidak begitu th krn jawaban dia tdk pasti dan malah tanya ke satpam yg ada di samping dia. Satpam itu blg "kl 0 brrti habis bang, sering² dicek aja, hari ini kapal cm 3 sampai jam 5 aja" dg nada yg tdk ramah. Akhirnya kita putuskan naik kapal tanpa kendaraan alias orgnya aja. Stlh sampai k tmpt tujuan, kami turun ke bawah sembari menunggu kapalnya bersandar dari situ lah kami melihat, bahwa tmpt yg harusnya penuh krn di aplikasi kuotanya sdh 0 tp kenyataannya kapal itu cm berisi setengah masih banyak space, hanya ada beberapa mobil dn motor, kalau alasannya adlh berat, sepertinya tdk jg, krn tdk banyak kendaraan besar yg bermuatan saat itu. Tolong dong, petugasnya lbh diperhatikan lg pemberi pelayanan di sana, bikin SOP kalau blm punya, biar punya standar, kalau udh punya SOP tolong dong perbaiki, tolong jg ajarkan bekerja sesuai SOP, apa lg d bidang pelayanan, suruh terapkan senyum dan keramahan. Dari sekian kali bolak balik ke sana baru kemarin dpt yg gabagus pelayanannya.

column6: [WAJIB BACA] Saya tidak suka karna pelabuhan kapal ini memonopoli harga taxi. Mereka tidak sanggup bersaing dan mendemo agar taxi online seperti grab dan gojek tidak boleh mengambil order di sini. Bahkan mereka memukul driver online & pelanggan kalau berani memesan di area pelabuhan. Mereka berkali-kali dan terus-menerus memanggil-manggil pelanggan & meminta memesan taxi mereka, di level yang sangat mengganggu. Walaupun sudah sepakat harga taxi, di tengah jalan mereka akan menaikkan harga sesuka hati dengan alasan tujuan jauh, mengintimidasi pelanggan dan memasang ekspresi wajah yang membuat pelanggan tidak nyaman. UNTUK ORANG BARU DI BATAM, APALAGI ANDA FOREIGNERS, bijaklah memilih transportasi. Ada layanan bus "trans batam" dari pemerintah, cara nya setelah keluar dari pelabuhan, jalan lurus sedikit, naik ke lantai 2 menggunakan lift/elevator atau tangga. Setelah benar-benar keluar (sampai dijalan aspal), jalan sedikit ke kiri dan terlihat halte bus. Tiket bus hanya tersedia cashless, bayar pakai QRIS. Biasanya saya turun di Mall BCS atau di area "jodoh" (persis di depan hotel pacific sekitaran harbour bay). Lanjutkan dengan memesan grab atau gojek ke tujuan anda. Saya tidak ingin membenci mereka tapi mereka sendiri yang membuat semua orang membenci mereka dengan tindakan anarkis dan pemaksaan.

column6: Kejadian kemarin saat saya hendak pulang dari Batam ke Selat Panjang melalui Pelabuhan Sekupang. Saat tiba di pelabuhan, saya menuju konter yang jelas-jelas bertuliskan “Dumai Line” untuk membeli tiket. Setelah membayar dan menerima tiket, saya heran karena tiket yang diberikan ternyata bertuliskan “Batam Jet”. Saya kemudian bertanya kepada petugas, “Kok Batam Jet? Saya mau naik Dumai Line.” Namun petugas tidak menjawab pertanyaan saya dan hanya mengatakan, “Kapal besar.” Saya kembali menegaskan bahwa saya ingin tiket Dumai Line, tetapi petugas hanya diam. Lalu petugas lain mengatakan bahwa uang tidak bisa ditransfer kembali karena pembayaran sudah dilakukan. Untungnya akhirnya uang saya dikembalikan secara tunai. Setelah itu saya membeli tiket di konter Dumai Line yang sebenarnya, yang berada tepat di sampingnya, dan mendapatkan tiket yang sesuai. Yang membuat saya semakin kesal, ternyata orang tua saya pernah mengalami kejadian serupa. Karena tidak terlalu mengenal tulisan, mereka baru mengetahui tiket yang dibeli bukan Dumai Line saat sudah hendak naik kapal dan diberitahu oleh petugas. Saya sebenarnya tidak berniat memposting hal ini. Namun karena kejadian yang sama juga dialami oleh orang tua saya, saya merasa perlu menyampaikan keluhan ini. Mohon kepada pihak Pelabuhan Sekupang untuk menindaklanjuti dan mengawasi praktik seperti ini agar tidak ada lagi penumpang yang mengalami kebingungan atau dirugikan, terutama orang tua dan penumpang yang kurang memahami perbedaan loket maupun nama operator kapal. Terima kasih.

column6: Terminal Feri Sekupang merupakan salah satu pelabuhan utama di Kota Batam yang melayani transportasi laut domestik dan internasional. Terletak di kawasan Sekupang, pelabuhan ini terbagi menjadi dua bagian, yaitu terminal domestik dan terminal internasional. Terminal domestik melayani rute antarpulau seperti ke Karimun, Tanjung Balai, Dumai, dan pulau-pulau di wilayah Riau , sementara terminal internasional melayani rute cepat ke Singapura dan Malaysia dengan waktu tempuh sekitar 45 menit. Fasilitas di Terminal Feri Sekupang tergolong lengkap dan modern. column6: Terminal feri internasional Sekupang telah berubah menjadi tempat yang suram. Hampir tidak ada layanan yang tersedia, pedagang telah tutup, karena kenaikan sewa sebesar 30%. Ini bukan cara untuk menarik penumpang yang membayar. Lebih baik berjalan kaki 3 menit ke terminal domestik untuk mendapatkan lebih banyak pilihan yang masuk akal. column6: Hati-hati dengan porter! Ini adalah kali kedua saya di terminal feri Sekupang dan biasanya setelah mendapatkan cap paspor dari Imigrasi Indonesia, saya berjalan untuk mendapatkan kartu kedatangan dengan kode QR untuk dipindai, langkah terakhir adalah memasukkan tas saya ke mesin sinar-X dan mengambilnya setelah melewati mesin. Biasanya bagasi akan berada di samping mesin sinar-X, tetapi entah kenapa saya tidak dapat menemukannya dan saya bertanya dan melihat bahwa bagasi berada di luar area penurunan bagasi. Ketika hendak mengambil bagasi saya, saya menyerahkan bukti penerimaan bagasi kepada porter, tetapi entah kenapa porter tersebut meminta uang! Saya mengatakan kepada mereka bahwa tidak ada yang meminta mereka untuk mengambil bagasi kami dan mengapa kami harus membayar untuk layanan yang tidak pernah kami minta bantuan siapa pun untuk memuat dan menurunkan bagasi kami, yang dapat kami lakukan sendiri. Jumlah yang mereka minta saya kira sekitar 40.000 hingga 100.000 rupiah. Saya tidak akan pernah mendukung layanan porter yang korup seperti itu dan saya langsung bersikap tegas dan mengatakan kepada mereka dalam bahasa Indonesia bahwa tidak ada yang namanya membayar kepada mereka. Memang benar, Batam memiliki salah satu terminal feri dengan korupsi terburuk. Saya tidak akan pernah mengunjungi Batam lagi karena pengalaman sekali itu akan menjadi yang terakhir, dan perlu diingat saya telah mengunjungi Batam setidaknya 6 kali dalam 10 tahun terakhir dan tidak ada yang berubah kecuali sistem yang korup. Ingat, jangan sampai tertipu dan membayar porter, cukup katakan tidak dengan tegas dan pergi. Diterjemahkan oleh Google ・ Lihat versi asli (Inggris)

column6: Beberapa speedboat berangkat dari sini ke Sumatra dan pulau-pulau sekitarnya. Kami naik satu ke Kuala Lumpur dengan harga 612.000 rupee yang lumayan mahal. Sayangnya, penerbangan ke Jakarta hampir lebih murah. Pelabuhannya sendiri sangat baik. Petugas di meja informasi ramah dan membantu. Staf di loket tiket agak terlalu bersemangat, tetapi kami tetap mendapatkan tiket. Ada restoran yang bagus di seberang jalan. Kapalnya penuh petualangan, cepat, dan stabil. Modelnya sangat tua, ditenagai oleh lima motor tempel yang luar biasa berisik, tetapi tampaknya bertenaga. Kami berangkat tepat pukul 10.00 pagi dan tiba di tujuan tepat pukul 17.00, termasuk istirahat makan siang selama setengah jam. Suara mesin dan pemutaran video yang terus-menerus keras dari ponsel sangat mengganggu. Orang-orang di sini tidak sopan dan tidak punya sopan santun. Setidaknya banyak dari mereka yang begitu. Bahkan beberapa awak kapal. Perjalanan menyusuri garis pantai hampir sepanjang perjalanan. Perahu berhenti beberapa kali dan menyeberangi sungai besar di pedalaman Sumatra. Hanya setengah jam terakhir yang membawa kami menyeberangi lautan lepas. Di Kuala Lumpur, kami disambut dengan hangat dan diizinkan berfoto selfie dengan pemuda setempat. Daerah ini sangat Muslim, dan kami harus mencari cukup lama sebelum sebuah hotel mau memberi kami kamar ganda tanpa perlu bukti pernikahan (meskipun kami sudah menikah selama 12 tahun). Kami tidak mengalami hal seperti itu di tempat lain di Indonesia. Diterjemahkan oleh Google ・ Lihat versi asli (Jerman)
